assumptions: World Body IR v0.1 runtime validator is normative
theorem.statement: Every RSR reference state originates from a verified World Body IR with stable identities and roots.
theorem.title: World-body physical well-formedness

assumptions: All quantities use safe integers or canonical strings
theorem.statement: A normalized physical state has exactly one canonical SHA-256 state root.
theorem.title: Canonical physical state root

theorem.statement: Body identifiers and fixture identifiers are unique in their declared scopes.
theorem.title: Unique body and fixture identity

assumptions: No authority teleport command targets static bodies
theorem.statement: A fixed-step transition does not change a static body transform.
theorem.title: Static body immutability

theorem.statement: Every dynamic body has strictly positive integral mass.
theorem.title: Positive dynamic mass

theorem.statement: The canonical contact identity is invariant under fixture order.
theorem.title: Contact identity symmetry

assumptions: categoryBits and maskBits are non-negative integers
theorem.statement: A collision pair is enabled only when both category-mask directions admit the pair.
theorem.title: Collision filter reciprocity

assumptions: Reference transition uses safe-integer fixed-step arithmetic
theorem.statement: Equal normalized state and command inputs produce equal successor roots.
theorem.title: Fixed-step transition determinism

assumptions: Inputs remain within JavaScript safe-integer range
theorem.statement: The reference transition maps the integer state domain back into the integer state domain.
theorem.title: Integer state closure

theorem.statement: A valid sealed snapshot restores the exact state root.
theorem.title: Snapshot restoration identity

theorem.statement: Authoritative event exactly-once keys are unique and bound to the active authority root.
theorem.title: Event identity uniqueness

assumptions: Commands carry stable tick, sequence, and id
theorem.statement: Replay from one state with one command multiset converges to one successor root.
theorem.title: Deterministic replay

theorem.statement: An authority frame root commits to every normalized body root.
theorem.title: Nested authority body-root binding

assumptions: World Body authority and presentation roots remain separate
theorem.statement: The physical authority state contains no visual mesh, material, shader, camera, or observer fields.
theorem.title: Presentation exclusion from authority state

assumptions: No acceleration or collision impulse in the reference step
Rounding error is at most half a millimetre per axis
theorem.statement: Per-axis displacement equals rounded velocity divided by tick rate for a command-free dynamic step.
theorem.title: Bounded fixed-step displacement

assumptions: Observable scope is worldId, tick, body identity, kind, and position
theorem.statement: The declared RSR observational refinement relation is reflexive at zero positional tolerance.
theorem.title: Refinement relation reflexivity

assumptions: The production adapter is total for the selected observable scope
Tolerance is declared, not inferred
theorem.statement: Any implementation trace satisfying the declared relation preserves the selected RSR observables within its explicit bound.
theorem.title: Adapter refinement sufficiency

assumptions: A real target backend and differential adapter are executed
theorem.statement: A target PhysX, Jolt, Chaos, Unity, or Unreal backend is observationally equivalent in the declared scope.
theorem.title: External physics backend equivalence

assumptions: World Body IR v0.1 runtime validator is normative
theorem.statement: Every VSR reference projection originates from a verified World Body IR.
theorem.title: World-body visual well-formedness

theorem.statement: Every projection carries the exact authority and physical source roots.
theorem.title: Projection source binding

theorem.statement: Visual objects and assets have unique stable identities.
theorem.title: Unique visual and asset identity

assumptions: Projection functions are pure
theorem.statement: Projection does not mutate authority or physical component roots.
theorem.title: Authority non-interference

assumptions: Presentation-only entities use the zero authority transform
theorem.statement: Every authoritative visual pose is the physical pose composed with the declared visual-only offset.
theorem.title: BodyMap transform law

theorem.statement: Observer capability sets contain no write, commit, or authorization authority.
theorem.title: Observer authority exclusion

assumptions: The reference frame requests only resident assets
theorem.statement: Every asset referenced by the reference projection is declared resident.
theorem.title: Resident asset completeness

theorem.statement: Equal World Body inputs produce equal presentation roots.
theorem.title: Deterministic projection

assumptions: Sample fraction is in [0,1]
theorem.statement: Every sampled position component lies in the closed interval between its two samples, up to integer rounding.
theorem.title: Temporal interpolation bound

theorem.statement: Temporal extrapolation applies no more than maximumExtrapolationTicks.
theorem.title: Bounded extrapolation

theorem.statement: Correction is none, blend, or snap according to the declared distance threshold.
theorem.title: Deterministic correction partition

assumptions: The World Body Render Graph validator is normative
theorem.statement: Every declared render graph is acyclic and free of initialization, ordering, and alias lifetime errors.
theorem.title: Render graph safety

theorem.statement: Every ordered read/write or write/write hazard has its deterministic declared barrier and no unjustified barrier.
theorem.title: Barrier completeness

theorem.statement: A visual-only offset may change a projection root but cannot change its authority or physical source roots.
theorem.title: Visual-offset source-root invariance

assumptions: This theorem covers only the declared diffuse reference term, not complete Cook-Torrance pixels
theorem.statement: For normalized non-negative inputs, the scaled diffuse term is non-negative and bounded by incoming radiance.
theorem.title: Non-negative bounded diffuse PBR

assumptions: Observable scope is authority root, entity identity, visual body identity, and position
theorem.statement: The declared VSR observable refinement relation is reflexive at zero positional tolerance.
theorem.title: Projection refinement reflexivity

assumptions: The production adapter is total for the selected observable scope
theorem.statement: Any implementation projection satisfying the declared relation preserves selected VSR observables within its explicit bound.
theorem.title: Adapter refinement sufficiency

assumptions: A real target adapter, texture path, shadows, pixel capture, and tolerance contract are executed
theorem.statement: A real browser/target GPU backend produces semantically and visually equivalent resources, commands, and pixels.
theorem.title: External GPU and pixel equivalence

assumptions: World Body IR v0.1 validator is normative
theorem.statement: A valid World Body document closes all seven root objects, BodyMap, Render Graph set, and the world root.
theorem.title: Seven-root closure

assumptions: Real RCL VM, target physics/backend, network recovery, browser GPU, pixels, and target hardware are all executed with independent oracles
theorem.statement: The complete declaration-to-RSR-to-network-to-VSR-to-real-GPU/VM/backend chain is differentially equivalent in its declared production scope.
theorem.title: Full external production differential

assumptions: Presentation-only entities explicitly omit physicalBodyRef
theorem.statement: Each declared entity has at most one physical reference, exactly one visual reference, and exactly one temporal policy reference.
theorem.title: BodyMap total functional binding

assumptions: Projection is pure and owns no commit capability
theorem.statement: Presentation binds authority and physical roots but cannot mutate either root.
theorem.title: Authority-presentation non-interference

theorem.statement: Every routed event delivery has one authority source and one unique delivery key; no route owns authority.
theorem.title: Single-source exactly-once event routing

assumptions: The transition adapter reseals World Body IR before projection
theorem.statement: After a physical transition, the projection source roots equal the new authority and physical roots.
theorem.title: Commuting authority-to-presentation transition

theorem.statement: Restoring a sealed physical snapshot recovers the exact post-transition state root without changing the base World Body root.
theorem.title: Snapshot rollback identity

assumptions: World Body Render Graph validator is normative
theorem.statement: Every World Body render graph is a valid DAG with initialized resources, ordered hazards, disjoint aliases, and complete barriers.
theorem.title: Generated render-graph safety closure

assumptions: Branches are candidate-only until an external authority commit
theorem.statement: Candidate branches share one immutable base root, diverge by their commands, and observer filtering changes no authority root.
theorem.title: Branch and observer isolation

assumptions: RSR and VSR adapters are total for their declared observables
Tolerance bounds are explicit
theorem.statement: If RSR and VSR refinement relations hold and the VSR source authority equals the implementation authority root, the selected joint observables refine.
theorem.title: Compositional refinement
